claim.scope_statement:
For the stated linear-type screening problem, additionally assume that the compact convex allocation set contains zero and that the continuous convex cost is nonnegative with C(0)=0. I claim an explicit two-sided comparison between the continuum optimal value and a finite-type convex program, and a construction converting any certified solution of that program into a globally IC/IR finite menu. With type-cell radius h, the resulting objective gap is at most the certified finite-program gap plus O(sqrt(h)), with constants given below. No Lipschitz bound on the cost or density is required for this analytic comparison when cell probabilities are exact.

For rational polytopes, a positive normalized rational polynomial density, and rational convex piecewise-affine cost, the construction gives a finite algorithm using exact cell integration and rational linear-program certificates. This is a theorem and algorithm specification, not a report of an executed numerical solver. It does not characterize exclusion or bunching, establish a new literature priority, or solve the whole research family.
